analysis.body:
Per the Census Bureau, the latest survey reading shows 36.5% of finance and insurance firms, NAICS 52, answered yes to using AI in the last two weeks. The prior period figure was 40.0%. The question was first asked in September 2023. This is the broad finance and insurance sector rather than banking alone, so it is the closest official adoption measure the material provides.

The page's framing notes that fraud detection and credit models are decades old in banking, while generative AI in service and compliance is the new frontier. The World of AI's Financial Models section tracks the 1,000 most-downloaded open financial models on the Hugging Face Hub, refreshed daily, with licence, downloads, and release date, and describes them as tuned for financial text. That points to a large open supply of financial language models, though the excerpts do not say how many banks deploy them.

Per the Evident AI Banking Index, major global banks are scored across dozens of quantitative maturity metrics, including talent, innovation, leadership, and transparency, making it the closest thing banking has to a public AI scoreboard. Per the Federal Reserve, credit and AML models operate under SR 11-7 model risk management guidance issued in 2011, and the letter is listed in the Fed's 2011 supervisory letters index. That means banking is the sector where AI governance predates the AI boom by more than a decade.

Per Treasury, its report on AI in financial services, covering uses, opportunities, and risks, frames the US supervisory conversation. A reader deciding whether to deploy should weigh the measured adoption rate in finance and insurance, the existing model risk rules, and the availability of open financial models, while noting that the material here does not report ROI evidence or where vendor spending concentrates.

https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-rel.brief: On International Anti-Corruption Day, Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control sanctioned 28 individuals and businesses tied to a Zimbabwe-based gold smuggling and money-laundering network led by Kamlesh Pattni. The Treasury says the scheme bribed officials, used trusted supporters to conceal ownership, and built a global web of companies to hide illicit activity, depriving Zimbabwe’s citizens of resource benefits while enriching corrupt officials and criminals. Acting Under Secretary Bradley T. Smith noted that “Corruption respects no borders” and that the action demonstrates a whole-of-government approach and collaboration with allies. The Treasury’s move is carried out under Executive Order 13818, which targets serious human-rights abuse and corruption worldwide. International Anti-Corruption Day, observed annually on December 9 since the 2003 UNCAC, aims to raise awareness of anti-corruption initiatives; the United Nations lists 189 parties to the convention.

https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisi.brief: This page lists the Federal Reserve Board of Governors’ 2011 supervision and regulation letters. It notes that a lock icon or https indicates a secure .gov connection and advises “Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites.” It also contains guidance on prior notices concerning dividend declarations by savings association subsidiaries of savings and loan holding companies.

https://theworldofai.org/ai-ecosystem/te.brief: The page lists the 1000 most-downloaded open financial models on the Hugging Face Hub, showing each model’s licence, download count, and release date, with the data refreshed daily. It also advertises books by Stephen R. Jordan, including “The Operating Discipline for AI Library™” series, now available on Amazon. In addition, the page catalogs a series of AI audit and assessment services such as the AI Business Enablement Audit™, AI Readiness & Performance Assessment™, AI Risk & Governance Review™, AI Efficiency & Process Optimization™, AI IT Security Audit™, AI IT Security Implementation & Strategy™, Secure by Design in the Age of AI™, Application Security in the Age of AI™, and the AI Lawyer. The information is presented as a straightforward inventory of resources and services.
